dockerfile
# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable and widely supported environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend to prevent prompts during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, runtime dependencies, and required utilities in a single layer.
# - build-essential, cmake, git: Core tools for compiling from source.
# - ca-certificates: For secure network connections (e.g., git clone).
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: For MPI (Message Passing Interface) support, essential for HPC.
# - libfftw3-dev: FFTW library, a common performance dependency for LAMMPS.
# - libgomp1: GNU OpenMP library, explicitly requested.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    libfftw3-dev \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    libgomp1 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set environment variables for running Open MPI in containerized environments like Docker/Kubernetes.
# - OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT*: Required to run MPI as the root user inside the container.
# - OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Works around a shared memory issue in some container runtimes.
# - OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows running more MPI processes than available physical cores.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1 \
    OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none \
    OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

# This RUN command encapsulates the entire build process to optimize layer usage.
# It clones from source, builds with specific packages, installs the binary,
# copies necessary example files, and then cleans up the source code.
RUN set -e && \
    # Create a temporary directory for the build process
    mkdir -p /tmp/build && cd /tmp/build && \
    # Clone the latest available branch of the LAMMPS repository.
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git && \
    cd lammps && \
    mkdir build && cd build && \
    # Configure the LAMMPS build using CMake.
    # - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Optimizes the build for performance.
    # - BUILD_MPI=on: Enables MPI support for distributed computing.
    # - PKG_REAXFF=on: Enables the ReaxFF package as required by the application name.
    # - PKG_OPENMP=on: Enables OpenMP for shared-memory parallelism on multi-core CPUs.
    cmake ../cmake \
        -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
        -D BUILD_MPI=on \
        -D PKG_REAXFF=on \
        -D PKG_OPENMP=on && \
    # Compile the source code using all available CPU cores for speed.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Install the compiled 'lmp' executable to a system-wide location (/usr/local/bin).
    # This ensures 'lmp' is available on the system PATH without symlinking, fulfilling the requirement.
    make install && \
    # Create the final application directory.
    mkdir -p /app && \
    # Copy all files from the requested example directory into the application directory.
    cp /tmp/build/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /app/ && \
    # Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size.
    cd / && rm -rf /tmp/build

# Purge build-time dependencies that are not needed for the final runtime image.
# This significantly reduces the final image size, making it more production-ready.
RUN apt-get purge -y --auto-remove build-essential cmake git libfftw3-dev libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get autoremove -y --purge && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the default working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /app

# Set the default command. The container will run 'lmp' by default.
# Users can append arguments to this entrypoint, e.g., 'docker run <image> -in in.hns'.
ENTRYPOINT ["lmp"]

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable and widely supported environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend to prevent prompts during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, runtime dependencies, and required utilities in a single layer.
# - build-essential, cmake, git: Core tools for compiling from source.
# - ca-certificates: For secure network connections (e.g., git clone).
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: For MPI (Message Passing Interface) support, essential for HPC.
# - libfftw3-dev: FFTW library, a common performance dependency for LAMMPS.
# - libgomp1: GNU OpenMP library, explicitly requested.
# - python3, python3-dev: (FIX) Required by the LAMMPS CMake build system, which was the cause of the previous build failure.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    libfftw3-dev \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    libgomp1 \
    python3 \
    python3-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set environment variables for running Open MPI in containerized environments like Docker/Kubernetes.
# - OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT*: Required to run MPI as the root user inside the container.
# - OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Works around a shared memory issue in some container runtimes.
# - OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows running more MPI processes than available physical cores.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1 \
    OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none \
    OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

# This RUN command encapsulates the entire build process to optimize layer usage.
# It clones from source, builds with specific packages, installs the binary,
# copies necessary example files, and then cleans up the source code.
RUN set -e && \
    # Create a temporary directory for the build process
    mkdir -p /tmp/build && cd /tmp/build && \
    # Clone the latest available branch of the LAMMPS repository.
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git && \
    cd lammps && \
    mkdir build && cd build && \
    # Configure the LAMMPS build using CMake.
    # - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Optimizes the build for performance.
    # - BUILD_MPI=on: Enables MPI support for distributed computing.
    # - PKG_REAXFF=on: Enables the ReaxFF package as required by the application name.
    # - PKG_OPENMP=on: Enables OpenMP for shared-memory parallelism on multi-core CPUs.
    cmake ../cmake \
        -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
        -D BUILD_MPI=on \
        -D PKG_REAXFF=on \
        -D PKG_OPENMP=on && \
    # Compile the source code using all available CPU cores for speed.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Install the compiled 'lmp' executable to a system-wide location (/usr/local/bin).
    # This ensures 'lmp' is available on the system PATH without symlinking, fulfilling the requirement.
    make install && \
    # Create the final application directory.
    mkdir -p /app && \
    # Copy all files from the requested example directory into the application directory.
    cp /tmp/build/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /app/ && \
    # Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size.
    cd / && rm -rf /tmp/build

# Purge build-time dependencies that are not needed for the final runtime image.
# This significantly reduces the final image size, making it more production-ready.
# (FIX) Added python3 and python3-dev to the purge list.
RUN apt-get purge -y --auto-remove build-essential cmake git libfftw3-dev libopenmpi-dev python3 python3-dev && \
    apt-get autoremove -y --purge && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the default working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /app

# Set the default command. The container will run 'lmp' by default.
# Users can append arguments to this entrypoint, e.g., 'docker run <image> -in in.hns'.
ENTRYPOINT ["lmp"]

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable and widely supported environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend to prevent prompts during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, runtime dependencies, and required utilities in a single layer.
# - build-essential, cmake, git: Core tools for compiling from source.
# - python3, python3-dev: Required by the modern LAMMPS CMake build system.
# - ca-certificates: For secure network connections (e.g., git clone).
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: For MPI (Message Passing Interface) support, essential for HPC.
# - libfftw3-dev: FFTW library, a common performance dependency for LAMMPS.
# - libgomp1: GNU OpenMP library, explicitly requested.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    python3 \
    python3-dev \
    ca-certificates \
    libfftw3-dev \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    libgomp1 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set environment variables for running Open MPI in containerized environments like Docker/Kubernetes.
# - OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT*: Required to run MPI as the root user inside the container.
# - OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: Works around a shared memory issue in some container runtimes.
# - OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe: Allows running more MPI processes than available physical cores.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1 \
    OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none \
    OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

# This RUN command encapsulates the entire build process to optimize layer usage.
# It clones from source, builds with specific packages, installs the binary,
# copies necessary example files, and then cleans up the source code.
RUN set -e && \
    # Create a temporary directory for the build process
    mkdir -p /tmp/build && cd /tmp/build && \
    # Clone the latest available branch of the LAMMPS repository.
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git && \
    cd lammps && \
    mkdir build && cd build && \
    # Configure the LAMMPS build using CMake.
    # - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Optimizes the build for performance.
    # - BUILD_MPI=on: Enables MPI support for distributed computing.
    # - PKG_REAXFF=on: Enables the ReaxFF package as required by the application name.
    # - PKG_OPENMP=on: Enables OpenMP for shared-memory parallelism on multi-core CPUs.
    cmake ../cmake \
        -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
        -D BUILD_MPI=on \
        -D PKG_REAXFF=on \
        -D PKG_OPENMP=on && \
    # Compile the source code using all available CPU cores for speed.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Install the compiled 'lmp' executable to a system-wide location (/usr/local/bin).
    # This ensures 'lmp' is available on the system PATH, fulfilling the requirement.
    make install && \
    # Create the final application directory.
    mkdir -p /app && \
    # Copy all files from the requested example directory into the application directory.
    cp /tmp/build/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /app/ && \
    # Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size.
    cd / && rm -rf /tmp/build

# Purge build-time dependencies that are not needed for the final runtime image.
# This significantly reduces the final image size, making it more production-ready.
RUN apt-get purge -y --auto-remove build-essential cmake git libfftw3-dev libopenmpi-dev python3-dev && \
    apt-get autoremove -y --purge && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the default working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /app

# Set the default command. The container will run 'lmp' by default.
# Users can append arguments to this entrypoint, e.g., 'docker run <image> -in in.hns'.
ENTRYPOINT ["lmp"]

        -D PKG_REAXFF=on \
        -D PKG_OPENMP=on && \
    # Compile the source code using all available CPU cores for speed.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Install the compiled 'lmp' executable to a system-wide location (/usr/local/bin).
    # This ensures 'lmp' is available on the system PATH, fulfilling the requirement.
    make install && \
    # Create the final application directory.
    mkdir -p /app && \
    # Copy all files from the requested example directory into the application directory.
    cp /tmp/build/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /app/ && \
    # Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size.
    cd / && rm -rf /tmp/build

# Purge build-time dependencies that are not needed for the final runtime image.
# This significantly reduces the final image size, making it more production-ready.
RUN apt-get purge -y --auto-remove build-essential cmake git libfftw3-dev libopenmpi-dev python3-dev && \
    apt-get autoremove -y --purge && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the default working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /app

# Set the default command. The container will run 'lmp' by default.
# Users can append arguments to this entrypoint, e.g., 'docker run <image> -in in.hns'.
ENTRYPOINT ["lmp"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is corrected to resolve an architecture mismatch
# and a structural error from a previous attempt.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-test
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Ensure all tasks run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # Match tasks to the vCPUs of the selected AMD instance for optimal performance.
  # Updated from 64 to 48 to match the c7a.12xlarge instance type.
  tasks: 48

  # Keep job pods for inspection after completion.
  cleanup: false

  # Pod specification for the Flux job, including node selection.
  # This structure is corrected from the previous version.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      # FIX: Switched from an ARM instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) to a high core-count AMD (amd64) instance.
      # Rationale: The "lmp: No such file or directory" error (exit 127) indicated the application
      # container does not have a working executable for the arm64 architecture.
      # Choosing c7a.12xlarge (48 vCPU) avoids this architecture mismatch.
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge

  # Container specification for the LAMMPS application.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # Command for the testing run, as specified in the task.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      launcher: false

  # Enforce strict schema validation for logs.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # FIX: Removed the ARM-specific flux configuration (arch and container image)
  # as it is no longer needed for the amd64 target node.

# This MiniCluster manifest is configured to resolve a "command not found" error
# by switching to a known-good ARM architecture and correcting the manifest structure.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-test
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size 1 ensures all tasks run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # Matching tasks to the number of vCPUs (64) on the selected ARM instance for optimal performance.
  tasks: 64
  # Keep job pods for inspection after completion.
  cleanup: false

  # Flux-specific settings required for the ARM architecture of hpc7g.16xlarge.
  flux:
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Container specification for the LAMMPS application.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # Using the command specified for the testing run.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      launcher: false

  # FIX: Corrected the manifest structure. Pod specifications are placed under `spec.pod`,
  # not `spec.jobspec`, to adhere to the v1alpha2 CRD schema.
  pod:
    # Setting restartPolicy to Never is best practice for batch jobs to inspect logs of failed pods.
    restartPolicy: Never
    # FIX: Selecting a high core-count, HPC-optimized ARM instance to resolve the suspected
    # architecture mismatch in the application container.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # Enforce strict schema validation for logs.
  logging:
    strict: true

# This MiniCluster manifest is corrected to resolve an architecture mismatch
# by switching from an ARM instance to a compatible AMD64 instance.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of our MiniCluster instance.
  name: lammps-reax-test
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Ensure the job runs on a single node.
  size: 1
  # Match the number of MPI tasks to the vCPUs of the selected AMD instance.
  tasks: 48
  # Disable cleanup to allow for log inspection on failure.
  cleanup: false
  # Set backoff limit to 1 as per instructions, preventing multiple retries.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Defines pod-level specifications. The structure is corrected to use `spec.pod`
  # instead of the invalid `spec.jobspec` for the v1alpha2 API.
  pod:
    # Set restart policy to Never to preserve failed pods for debugging.
    restartPolicy: Never
    # FIX: Switched from an ARM instance to an AMD64 instance to resolve the
    # "lmp: No such file or directory" error caused by an architecture mismatch.
    # c7a.12xlarge is chosen for its high core count (48 vCPU).
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge

  # Define the application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # Use the correct testing command as specified in the task instructions.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # This is the main application container, not a launcher.
      launcher: false

  # Enforce strict schema validation for logs.
  logging:
    strict: true

# This MiniCluster manifest is corrected to resolve a structural error and
# ensure the job runs on the correct architecture with the specified test command.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-test
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # Match tasks to the vCPU count (48) of the selected AMD instance.
  tasks: 48

  # Set backoff limit to 1, preventing multiple retries on failure.
  backoffLimit: 1
  # Keep job pods for inspection after completion.
  cleanup: false
  # Enforce strict schema validation for logs.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # FIX: Pod specifications are placed under `spec.pod` for the v1alpha2 API.
  # The previous use of `spec.jobspec` was incorrect and caused the nodeSelector
  # to be ignored, leading to a likely architecture mismatch and command failure.
  pod:

# This MiniCluster manifest is corrected to resolve an operating system mismatch
# between the application container and the Flux runner container.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-test
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # Set tasks to match the vCPU count of the selected instance (c7a.12xlarge has 48 vCPUs).
  tasks: 48

  # Set the backoff limit to 1 per instructions. If it fails once, do not retry.
  backoffLimit: 1
  # Keep job pods for inspection after completion.
  cleanup: false

  # FIX: Define the Flux runner container to match the application container's OS (Ubuntu 22.04).
  # This resolves the "lmp: No such file or directory" error by ensuring shared library compatibility.
  flux:
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/rse-ops/flux-view:ubuntu-22.04

  # Defines pod-level specifications. The structure is corrected to use `spec.pod`
  # as required by the v1alpha2 API, instead of the invalid `spec.jobspec`.
  pod:
    # Set restartPolicy to Never to inspect logs on failure.
    restartPolicy: Never
    # Select the AMD instance type to match the container's architecture.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge

  # Define the application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # Use the required testing command as specified in the task instructions.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      launcher: false

  # Enforce strict schema validation for logs.
  logging:
    strict: true

      # Using the testing command as specified in the primary task instructions.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      launcher: false

# This MiniCluster manifest is corrected to resolve a "command not found" error
# by placing the pod specification in the correct location for the v1alpha2 API.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Using a standard name for the testing job.
  name: lammps-reax-test
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Keep pods and logs after completion for inspection.
  cleanup: false
  # Run on a single node as required.
  size: 1
  # Match tasks to the vCPU count of the selected instance for optimal performance.
  tasks: 48

  # Main application container configuration.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # Command for the testing run, as specified by the task instructions.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # This is the main application container, not a launcher.
      launcher: false

  # Enable strict logging for better debuggability.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod-level specifications.
  # FIX: The analysis suggesting `spec.jobspec` is incorrect for the v1alpha2 API.
  # Pod settings must be placed directly under `spec.pod` to be applied correctly.
  # This ensures the job is scheduled on the correct high-performance instance,
  # preventing architecture mismatches that cause "command not found" errors.
  pod:
    # Set restartPolicy to Never to preserve failed pods for log inspection.
    restartPolicy: Never
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge

# This MiniCluster manifest is corrected to resolve a "command not found" error.
# The fix addresses the manifest's structure, ensuring it adheres to the v1alpha2 API schema.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-test
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The MiniCluster will run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # Match tasks to the 48 vCPUs on the selected AMD instance.
  tasks: 48
  # Keep pods and logs for debugging after completion/failure.
  cleanup: false

  # Define the application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # Use the specified command for the testing run.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # This is the main application container, not a launcher.
      launcher: false

  # Enable strict logging for better diagnostics.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod-level specifications.
  # FIX: The provided analysis incorrectly suggested nesting pod specs under 'jobspec'.
  # For the v1alpha2 API, these settings must be placed directly under 'spec.pod'.
  # This correction ensures the nodeSelector is applied, preventing the architecture
  # mismatch that caused the "command not found" error.
  pod:
    # Schedule the job on an AMD instance to ensure architecture compatibility.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge
    # Set restart policy to Never to inspect logs of failed pods.
    restartPolicy: Never

# This MiniCluster manifest is corrected based on an analysis of previous failures.
# It uses the `spec.pod` field as defined in the v1alpha2 CRD schema to ensure
# pod specifications like nodeSelector are correctly applied.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-test
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Ensure the job runs on a single node.
  size: 1
  # Match tasks to the vCPU count of the selected instance (c7a.12xlarge has 48 vCPUs).
  tasks: 48

  # Keep pods on failure for log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  # Enable strict logging for better diagnostics.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Set backoffLimit to 1, preventing the job from retrying if it fails.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # FIX: Correctly placing pod specifications under 'spec.pod' as required by the v1alpha2 CRD.
  # Previous errors cited conflicting structures; the provided schema confirms 'spec.pod' is correct.
  pod:
    # Set restart policy to Never to allow inspection of failed pod logs.
    restartPolicy: Never
    # Select the AMD instance type to ensure architecture compatibility.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge

  # Define the application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # Using the testing command as explicitly required by the current task instructions.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # This is the main application container, not a launcher.
      launcher: false
